Create point geometries from longitude and latitude

Source: R/sfc_point.R
step_sfc_point.Rd

step_sfc_point() creates a specification of a recipe step that will combine a longitude column and a latitude column into a single point geometry column (an sfc column, see sf::st_sfc()).

Usage

step_sfc_point(
  recipe,
  lon,
  lat,
  role = "predictor",
  trained = FALSE,
  crs = 4326,
  name = "geometry",
  keep_original_cols = FALSE,
  skip = FALSE,
  id = rand_id("sfc_point")
)

Arguments

recipe

A recipe object. The step will be added to the sequence of operations for this recipe.

lon, lat

Bare names of the columns holding the longitude (x) and latitude (y) coordinates. Each must select exactly one numeric column. See recipes::selections() for more details.

role

Not used by this step since no new variables are created.

trained

A logical to indicate if the quantities for preprocessing have been estimated.

crs

The coordinate reference system of the coordinates, in any form accepted by sf::st_crs(). Defaults to 4326, WGS 84 longitude and latitude in degrees.

name

A single string, the name of the new geometry column. Defaults to "geometry".

keep_original_cols

A logical to keep the original longitude and latitude columns after the geometry column is created. Defaults to FALSE.

skip

A logical. Should the step be skipped when the recipe is baked by bake()? While all operations are baked when prep() is run, some operations may not be able to be conducted on new data (e.g. processing the outcome variable(s)). Care should be taken when using skip = TRUE as it may affect the computations for subsequent operations.

id

A character string that is unique to this step to identify it.

Value

An updated version of recipe with the new step added to the sequence of existing steps (if any).

Details

Rows where either coordinate is missing get an empty point (POINT EMPTY).

Tidying

When you tidy() this step, a tibble is returned with columns terms, argument, and id:

terms

character, the selectors or variables selected

argument

character, either "lon" or "lat"

id

character, id of this step

Examples

library(recipes)
data(ames, package = "modeldata")

rec <- recipe(Sale_Price ~ Longitude + Latitude, data = ames) |>
  step_sfc_point(lon = Longitude, lat = Latitude)

rec <- prep(rec)

bake(rec, new_data = NULL)
#> # A tibble: 2,930 × 2
#>    Sale_Price             geometry
#>         <int>          <POINT [°]>
#>  1     215000 (-93.61975 42.05403)
#>  2     105000 (-93.61976 42.05301)
#>  3     172000 (-93.61939 42.05266)
#>  4     244000 (-93.61732 42.05125)
#>  5     189900  (-93.63893 42.0609)
#>  6     195500 (-93.63893 42.06078)
#>  7     213500 (-93.63379 42.06298)
#>  8     191500 (-93.63383 42.06073)
#>  9     236500 (-93.63285 42.06112)
#> 10     189000 (-93.63907 42.05919)
#> # ℹ 2,920 more rows

tidy(rec, number = 1)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 3
#>   terms     argument id             
#>   <chr>     <chr>    <chr>          
#> 1 Longitude lon      sfc_point_UUEdL
#> 2 Latitude  lat      sfc_point_UUEdL

# Reference data for distance, nearest, count and join steps can be derived
# from ames itself. Hold out some homes as reference points so they do not
# overlap the rows being transformed (otherwise nearest distances are 0).
pts <- sf::st_as_sf(
  ames[, c("Sale_Price", "Year_Built", "Neighborhood", "Longitude", "Latitude")],
  coords = c("Longitude", "Latitude"),
  crs = 4326
)
held_out <- sample(nrow(ames), 100)
reference_points <- pts[held_out, ]
training <- ames[-held_out, ]

# Convex hull of the homes in each neighborhood with at least 3 homes
by_hood <- split(sf::st_geometry(pts), pts$Neighborhood)
by_hood <- by_hood[lengths(by_hood) >= 3]
reference_polygons <- sf::st_sf(
  Neighborhood = names(by_hood),
  geometry = sf::st_sfc(
    lapply(by_hood, \(x) sf::st_convex_hull(sf::st_union(x))[[1]]),
    crs = 4326
  )
)

# Hand-picked points: Iowa State University campus and downtown Ames
fixed_points <- sf::st_sfc(
  sf::st_point(c(-93.6465, 42.0267)),
  sf::st_point(c(-93.6199, 42.0347)),
  crs = 4326
)
